grade.rationale: The command structure is readable and the supplied build analyzer found no compilation issues, but the scan command can incorrectly pass when review metadata is missing. Argument parsing and report error handling also have correctness gaps that can produce misleading behavior.

summary: The CLI is generally straightforward, but its scan exit status does not fail on missing reviews, undermining use as a CI quality gate. Numeric option parsing mutates the argument index before validation, report-related I/O failures escape the intended error handling, and the review command lacks the help behavior provided by the other commands. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied.

grade.rationale: A scan containing missing review metadata can return success, and malformed numeric option values can be reinterpreted as positional arguments.
The code is organized into command-specific methods, but repetitive hand-written parsing and exception filters make consistent behavior difficult to maintain.
Names and command flow are generally clear, though inconsistent help handling and misleading diagnostics for invalid numeric values reduce predictability.
Most expected failures map to exit code 2 with concise diagnostics, but report file and filesystem I/O exceptions can escape the command-level handler.
Static console access and direct construction of runners, scanners, stores, and evaluators make isolated command tests cumbersome. Coverage remains unknown.

findings.title: Missing review metadata does not fail the scan
findings.description: The exit status tests only StaleCount. If files are reported as missing but none are stale, the command prints the missing entries and nevertheless exits successfully. This can allow unreviewed files to pass a CI quality gate.
findings.recommendation: Return exit code 1 when either stale or missing files exist, or explicitly document and expose an option if missing metadata is intentionally non-blocking.

findings.title: Invalid numeric option values are reinterpreted as positional arguments
findings.description: Both parsers increment index inside int.TryParse. When parsing fails, execution continues through the same if/else chain with args[index] now referring to the invalid value. That value can consequently become the review file or report repository path instead of producing the intended invalid-option error.
findings.recommendation: Inspect args[index + 1] without changing index, throw a targeted ArgumentException when parsing fails, and increment index only after successful validation. Consider extracting a shared numeric-option parser.

findings.title: Report I/O failures escape the command error handler
findings.description: RunReportAsync reads stored reports and writes optional output files, but its exception filter does not include IOException. Failures such as a full disk, broken output path, or read error therefore bypass the intended "quality report failed" diagnostic and exit-code-2 behavior.
findings.recommendation: Handle IOException in the report command's expected-error filter, and consider handling UnauthorizedAccessException if permission failures should receive the same CLI diagnostic.

findings.title: The review command treats help flags as errors
findings.description: Unlike analyze, report, security, boundaries, and flow, RunReviewAsync immediately parses its arguments. Consequently, `quality review --help` and `quality review -h` are reported as unexpected arguments rather than displaying review usage and returning success.
findings.recommendation: Add an initial help-flag branch to RunReviewAsync and a dedicated PrintReviewUsage method, consistent with the other subcommands.
